transcript.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hi, we're getting close to this month's limit. How much have we used so far, which day did we use the most, and do we have any credits to cover overage? When we hit the limit, will requests keep working and incur overage charges, and what error will our requests get? Org pebble-ai.

{"name": "usage-reconciliation", "steps": "1. Collect: org, the request ids, their HTTP status, when it happened and the timezone they used, and how they counted (`checks_done`: filters, tokenizer, retries, timeouts). Ask in one `ask_developer` call for what's missing.
2. Read in one round: `account_overview`, `usage_lookup` for the request ids, and `search_knowledge` for how billed tokens are counted and how retries, cancellation, caching, console delay and exports work.
3. Compare console facts with what they report: UTC time vs their timezone, `http_status`, `billed_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, and `line_id`/`invoice_id` (null = not on a Redwood invoice line yet, or billed elsewhere, e.g. by a marketplace; check the account's billing channel and the policy for that channel).
4. If a current page explains the difference (counting method, retries, cancellations, caching, timezone or filter cut, late or prior-period usage, console delay), explain it with their numbers. No case. Check which version of a rule applies to the request's date and product: billing months follow the account's billing timezone for usage from the date the close calendar gives; missing-usage thresholds depend on when the request was made (pipeline cut-over) and on the endpoint (some batch endpoints have their own delay); an incident status card may cover the time. Use `at_billing_timezone` from `usage_lookup`.
5. If the difference remains after those rules, or successful usage is still missing after the threshold that applies (before it, say when to check again and open no case), route it with `billing-handoff` to the team the routing passage names, with request ids, statuses, UTC window and what was checked."}

{"name": "payments-and-credits", "steps": "Failed payment
1. Get the invoice, the decline code, and when it failed with the timezone they used (`ask_developer` once for what's missing). Convert the time to UTC.
2. `search_knowledge` for the payment-processor incident procedure and for incident status cards for payment failures around that date (e.g. "INC card payments failing <month year>"). Read each card's window (UTC).
3. Inside a published window (the boundaries count as inside): the time decides, not the decline code. Name the incident, say the payment will be retried automatically and when retries complete, that they need do nothing, and that no late fees apply. No case. If this incident's notice gives no completion date, work it out from the usual schedule: search the earlier payment-processor incident notices, compare each window's end with its "last retries completed" date, apply that gap to this window's end, and say it is based on the usual schedule.
4. Outside every window, failed again after retries completed, or charged twice after retries: open the case the routing page names with invoice, decline code and failure time.
5. Card changes: Support never takes or repeats card numbers and doesn't change payment methods. Point them to Console billing settings; no case. If they shared a number, tell them not to send card details.

Overdue, late fees, suspension
- Use the current collections/dunning pages (check the effective year and whether the account pays by card or by invoice) and the account's invoice status from the console. Payments failed in an incident window are not overdue until retries finish.

Credit balance and expiry
1. `account_overview`: quote the balance from `credits` (the credit ledger), the balance and expiry date of each grant, not only the total. Confirm with `search_knowledge` which table policy says to quote if anything looks inconsistent.
2. Cash-out, refund of credits, restoring an expired credit, or another exception: explain the policy, promise nothing, and route the ask as the credit-ledger/routing pages say. Promo or workshop codes: follow their page (usually no case)."}

## Purpose
What happens when a Free workspace uses up its monthly included usage.
## Limits
- Free includes a fixed monthly amount of billed tokens and requests.
- Free has no overage: nothing beyond the included usage is ever charged, and Free workspaces never get an invoice.
## At the limit
Once a Free workspace reaches its monthly limit, further requests are rate-limited: the API returns HTTP `429` with error code `quota_exceeded` and a `Retry-After` header. Requests work again when the next month starts. To keep sending requests sooner, the customer upgrades to a paid plan.

  - Subscription fee (Builder)

Soft limit issues 429 with header X-Quota-Action: slow-down and offers Retry-After. If soft limit persists for >10s, platform escalates to hard 429 with X-Quota-Blocked.\n3) burst_pool (grace): Rolling 24h pool that replenishes linearly. When monthly_budget is near exhaustion, burst_pool provides allowance up to configured percentage of monthly_budget."}, {"source": "linear/design/PM-9031-tiered-burst-quotas-overage-grace-periods", "kind": "case record or discussion", "title": "PM-9031: Tiered burst quotas, soft/hard rate limits and overage billing policy", "status": "In Review", "updated": "2025-03-05", "text": "[requirements]
Define three quota layers per plan: baseline steady-state quota (monthly window), burst buffer (short-term allowance measured in tokens and requests), and per-second soft rate limit
Soft limits should throttle with controlled retries and informative headers, not immediate 429 hard failures until burst buffer exhausted or soft limit exceeded for >30s
Hard limits remain enforced for safety (abuse/fraud) and Dedicated customers can opt for hard-only behavior
Overage-enabled plans will automatically bill at a defined overage rate after monthly quota exhaustion; opt-out plans will block traffic and show a grace window notification
Console: show real-time quota burn, projected date-to-exhaust at current rate, burst buffer usage, and one-click opt-in for overage billing
API responses must include: X-Quota-Remaining, X-Burst-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, and a machine-readable reason for throttling (soft_throttle | hard_limit | quota_exhausted)"}, {"source": "linear/design/PM-9031-tiered-burst-quotas-overage-grace-periods", "kind": "case record or discussion", "title": "PM-9031: Tiered burst quotas, soft/hard rate limits and overage billing policy", "status": "In Review", "updated": "2025-03-05", "text": "Billing exports include overage line items with plan id and unit pricing and reconcile to invoices in staging environment
[billing_acceptance_criteria]
When a hosted account exhausts monthly baseline and has overage enabled, an overage invoice line is created automatically at the next billing run and shows items: units, unit price, and total
If overage is disabled, customer receives console notification and API calls are blocked with a clear error code: quota_exhausted_no_overage
Grace period: accounts that newly enable overage mid-cycle receive a configurable 48h grace window where overage is tracked but not billed; billing shows a 'grace' flag in staging exports
Proration: when a customer upgrades mid-cycle to a higher plan, remaining quota is prorated and overage thresholds are recomputed; tests must show correct ledger adjustments
Billing ledger and Console usage must reconcile within 2% for tokens and 3% for embeddings across a 7-day synthetic test"}, {"source": "confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/api-error-reference-2027", "kind": "policy/procedure page", "title": "API Error Reference (2027)", "status": "published", "updated": "2027-02-10", "text": "| 413 | `payload_too_large` | The request exceeds the model's context window or 20 MB | Shorten the input |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | Requests or tokens per minute above the workspace's rate limit, on any plan | Retry after the `Retry-After` header; spread traffic |
| 500 | `internal_error` | An unexpected server error | Retry with backoff; report the `request_id` if it persists |
| 503 | `overloaded` | Temporary capacity shortage in the region | Retry with backoff or use another region |
## Rate limits are not quotas
`429 rate_limited` is about speed: too many requests or tokens in a minute. It clears within a minute. A quota is about volume over a month and is reported with its own status above. Don't tell a customer to wait a minute for a quota error, or to upgrade for a rate limit unless they need a higher rate."}]}

## Invoice periods and billing timezones
Until February 2027 every invoice period ran on UTC. From March 2027 usage onward, an account's invoice period runs from midnight to midnight in the account's billing timezone (`billing_timezone` on the account record; UTC unless set). A request belongs to the billing month, and to the invoice line, in which its timestamp falls in that timezone. For an account on America/Los_Angeles, a request at 03:00 UTC on 1 April 2027 is 20:00 on 31 March local time, so it is March usage and is billed on the March invoice.

## Purpose
This page sets the 2027 monthly close for usage-based invoices: when each month's invoices are cut, which usage lands in which invoice period, and how late usage is handled. Billing Ops, Telemetry and Support use it when a customer asks what a month's invoice covers.
## Monthly close calendar
| Business day | Step | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| BD1 | Usage for the closed month is frozen in the metering warehouse | Telemetry |
| BD2 | Usage is rated against the account's price book and invoice lines are drafted | Billing Ops |
| BD3 | Variance review: lines more than 25% above the prior month are checked against usage | Billing Ops |
| BD4 | Invoices are issued and autopay is attempted on the due date shown on the invoice | Billing Ops |
| BD5 | Revenue for the month is booked and the period is closed | Accounting |"}, {"source": "google_drive/shared_drives/customer-success/qbr-token-exposure-scenarios-and-alert-playbook", "kind": "policy/procedure page", "title": "QBR Token Exposure Scenarios & Alert Playbook", "status": "in_review", "updated": "2026-02-14", "text": "- Per-route 95th-percentile tokens threshold breach -> create task for eng to evaluate batching/caching opportunities

- Daily budget = committed_monthly_budget / 30
- Tokens remaining in month = (committed_budget - spent_so_far) / cost_per_1k_tokens * 1000
- Runway weeks = tokens_remaining / average_weekly_token_burn

SELECT date, api_key, SUM(input_tokens + output_tokens) AS tokens
FROM `redwood_prod.logs.tokens`
WHERE date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 90 DAY) AND CURRENT_DATE()
GROUP BY date, api_key
ORDER BY date DESC
- top_routes_last_30d:
SELECT route, SUM(tokens) as tokens FROM `redwood_prod.logs.tokens`
WHERE date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
GROUP BY route ORDER BY tokens DESC LIMIT 10"}, {"source": "confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/usage-insights-api-contract", "kind": "policy/procedure page", "title": "Usage Insights API Contract (v1)", "status": "published", "updated": "2026-02-16", "text": "h2. Billing consistency and rounding
* total_cost is returned as a decimal number in the workspace billing currency.
* Totals are expected to reconcile with billing within tolerance:
  * Daily range: <= 0.5%
  * Hourly range: <= 1.0% (more sensitive to late events)
* The API returns *unrounded* values to 1/10000 currency unit internally; clients should display with 2 decimal places.
h1. GET /v1/usage-insights/top-drivers
Returns top cost drivers and “what changed” explanations for the selected window compared to a prior period.
h2. Query parameters
Required:
* workspace_id
Time window (choose one):
* start_at + end_at OR lookback
Optional:
* project_id, environment, deployment_mode, region
* route (if set, provides drivers within a route)
* model/model_family/model_version (if set, provides drivers within a model bucket)

[body]
## Purpose
What happens when a Free workspace uses up its monthly included usage.
## Limits
- Free includes a fixed monthly amount of billed tokens and requests.
- Free has no overage: nothing beyond the included usage is ever charged, and Free workspaces never get an invoice.

| HTTP status | `error.code` | Cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | Malformed JSON, unknown parameter, or a value out of range | Fix the request; don't retry unchanged |
| 401 | `invalid_api_key` | Missing, revoked or mistyped API key | Check the key in Console > API keys |
| 402 | `quota_exceeded` | A Free workspace used its monthly included amount, or a paid workspace with overage disabled reached its hard limit | Add a payment method or upgrade in Console billing settings; Free requests work again when the next month starts |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | The key's project can't use this model or region | Ask a workspace admin to grant access |
| 404 | `model_not_found` | Unknown or retired model name | Use a model from the models list |
| 409 | `idempotency_conflict` | An `Idempotency-Key` was reused with a different body | Use a new key for a new request |
| 413 | `payload_too_large` | The request exceeds the model's context window or 20 MB | Shorten the input |"}, {"source": "confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/hosted-api-packages-free-tier-and-overage-policy", "kind": "policy/procedure page", "title": "Hosted API Packages: Free Tier, Included Usage, and Overage Policy", "status": "published", "updated": "2026-02-26", "text": "- One Free workspace per legal entity by default (fraud/abuse controls may restrict).
